problems.title: Infinite Prime Nim losses
problems.words: Prime Nim has infinitely many losing pile sizes (a known theorem, since primes have arbitrarily large gaps). Show they are rare.
problems.math: Let $L=\{n: G(n)=0\}$ for the subtraction game with prime moves ($|L|=\infty$ is known). Prove $L$ has natural density $0$.

problems.title: Mod-3 Collatz map
problems.words: Divide by 3 when you can; otherwise double and add or subtract 1. Find all loops below a billion.
problems.math: Let $h(n)=n/3$ if $3\mid n$, $2n+1$ if $n\equiv1$, $2n-1$ if $n\equiv2 \pmod 3$. Classify all cycles of $h$ meeting $[1,10^9]$.

problems.title: Quarter-tone all-interval rows
problems.words: Count the tone rows in 24-note tuning that use every interval exactly once.
problems.math: Count permutations of $\mathbb{Z}_{24}$ whose successive differences are all distinct nonzero residues, and find their growth rate for $\mathbb{Z}_{2m}$.

problems.title: Small Keller maps in 3D
problems.words: The 2026 counterexamples to the Jacobian conjecture have fairly high degree. Is there one of degree 5 or less?
problems.math: Decide whether some $F:\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ with $\deg F\le5$ and $\det DF\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ has no polynomial inverse.

problems.title: Random walk on the hat tiling
problems.words: A random walker steps between neighbouring hat tiles. How likely is it to be back home after n steps?
problems.math: For simple random walk on the hat adjacency graph, prove $p_{2n}(o,o)\sim c/n$ and compute $c$.

problems.title: Monotile assembly threshold
problems.words: With one tile shape, deciding whether a region can be tiled is easy in some cases; with many shapes it is hard. Find the smallest number of shapes where it becomes hard.
problems.math: Find the least $t$ such that some fixed set of $t$ polygons makes "does this finite region admit an exact tiling?" NP-complete, and prove all sets of fewer polygons give polynomial-time problems.

problems.title: Spherical sofa
problems.words: Find the biggest shape that turns a right-angled corner in a width-1 hallway drawn on a large sphere.
problems.math: On the sphere of radius 10, determine the maximal area of a set admissible in the width-1 right-angled geodesic corridor.

problems.title: Largest-factor Collatz heights
problems.words: For almost every start, the largest-factor Collatz orbit never climbs past a fixed power of where it started.
problems.math: Prove there is $C$ with $\max_k f^k(n)\le n^C$ for a density-1 set of $n$.

problems.title: Fire on a random planet
problems.words: Fire spreads on a random planar map. Find how fast firefighting budgets must grow.
problems.math: On the uniform infinite planar triangulation, determine the minimal growth exponent $a$ such that budgets $k_t=t^{a}$ contain a fire almost surely.

problems.title: Kakeya for hats
problems.words: What is the smallest region in which you can rotate a hat tile through every orientation?
problems.math: Determine $\inf$ area of sets containing a translate of every rotation of the hat polygon.

problems.title: Sudoku transversals
problems.words: In every completed big Sudoku, find a set of cells with one in each row, each column and each symbol.
problems.math: Prove every $n^2\times n^2$ Sudoku grid, viewed as a Latin square, has a transversal.

problems.title: Petersen Ramsey multiplicity
problems.words: In any two-coloring of a huge complete graph, how many single-color copies of the Petersen graph must appear, at least?
problems.math: Determine the Ramsey multiplicity constant $\lim_n \min_{\text{2-col}} \#\text{mono } P / \#P \text{ in } K_n$ for the Petersen graph $P$.

problems.title: Icosahedral monotile
problems.words: Find a single 3D tile that fills space and forces five-fold, icosahedral symmetry in every tiling.
problems.math: Find $T\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ tiling space such that every tiling by $T$ has icosahedral symmetry in its hull, or prove none exists.

problems.title: Hat opaque set
problems.words: Find the shortest set of walls that blocks every straight line through the hat tile.
problems.math: Determine the minimal total length of an opaque set for the hat polygon.

problems.title: Smallest force for blow-up
problems.words: How weak can the push be and still make viscous fluid blow up?
problems.math: Find the optimal exponent $a$ with $\inf\{\|f\|_{L^\infty}: \text{NS from rest blows up}\}\asymp \nu^{a}$.

problems.title: Firebreak with wind
problems.words: How long must a firebreak be to save a round town from a wind-driven fire?
problems.math: For front speed $a+b\cos\theta$ and a disc town at distance $D$, find the minimal length of a curve built at speed $\sigma$ that protects the town.

problems.title: Isoperimetric sofa
problems.words: Among sofas with a fixed perimeter, find the one with largest area that turns the corner.
problems.math: For each $L$, maximize area over corridor-admissible sets of perimeter $\le L$.

problems.title: Spectre vs hat dimers
problems.words: Show the spectre tiling and the hat tiling have different domino-covering entropies.
problems.math: Prove the dimer entropies per vertex of the spectre and hat adjacency graphs differ.

problems.title: Doubled-twin constant
problems.words: Assuming deep but standard conjectures, find the exact count of doubled twins up to x.
problems.math: Assuming the Elliott–Halberstam conjecture, prove a lower bound $\gg x/(\log x)^4$ for doubled twins with $p$ and one other form prime.

problems.title: Pipe-bend sofa, exact
problems.words: Find and prove the optimal solid for a round pipe with a right-angle bend.
problems.math: Determine the maximal volume and an optimizer for the diameter-1 circular pipe with a right-angle bend.

problems.title: Sofa with a pillar
problems.words: A thin pillar stands in the corner of the hallway. Find the best sofa that gets around it.
problems.math: Determine the optimal sofa for the width-1 corridor with a point obstacle at $(1/2,1/2)$ from the outer corner.

problems.title: Three-pile shuffle cutoff
problems.words: Random three-pile shuffles mix a deck suddenly, after a precise number of shuffles. Find it.
problems.math: For random compositions of uniformly chosen 3-pile shuffles on $3n$ cards, prove total-variation cutoff at $c\log n$ and find $c$.

problems.title: Smooth shifted primes in two bases
problems.words: Find infinitely many primes p for which p − 1 has only small prime factors and p has no digit 7.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many 7-free primes $p$ with $P(p-1)\le p^{0.3}$.

problems.title: Square-sum connectivity
problems.words: Show the square-sum graph cannot be split by removing fewer vertices than its smallest degree.
problems.math: Prove $\kappa(S_N)=\delta(S_N)$ for all large $N$.

problems.title: Square-sum labelling of caterpillars
problems.words: Label the vertices of a tree with 1 to n so that every edge sums to a perfect square. Show every caterpillar of maximum degree 3 can be done, once it is large.
problems.math: Prove every caterpillar with $n\ge n_0$ vertices and maximum degree $\le3$ admits a bijection $V\to[n]$ with $\ell(u)+\ell(v)$ a square for every edge $uv$.

problems.title: Counting square-sum chains
problems.words: Count the ways to line up 1 to N with neighbours summing to squares. Find the leading growth.
problems.math: Let $h(N)$ be the number of Hamiltonian paths of $S_N$. Prove $\log h(N)=(\tfrac12+o(1))N\log N$.

problems.title: Seven-free Beatty primes
problems.words: Show infinitely many primes of the form ⌊n√2⌋ contain no digit 7.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many primes $p=\lfloor n\sqrt2\rfloor$ with no decimal digit 7.

problems.title: Seven-free Chen primes in progressions
problems.words: Show infinitely many seven-free primes p in every allowable residue class have p + 2 with at most three prime factors.
problems.math: For each $q$ and admissible $a$, prove infinitely many 7-free primes $p\equiv a\ (q)$ with $\Omega(p+2)\le3$.

problems.title: Largest factor of the midpoint
problems.words: For consecutive primes p < q, look at the largest prime factor of (p + q)/2. Show it exceeds p^0.5 for a positive fraction.
problems.math: Prove $\#\{n\le x: P(\tfrac{p_n+p_{n+1}}2)>p_n^{1/2}\}\gg \pi(x)$.

problems.title: Seven-free square-sum chains
problems.words: Take only the numbers up to N with no digit 7. Show they can be lined up so neighbours always sum to perfect squares, for large N.
problems.math: Let $A_N=\{n\le N: 7\notin n\}$. Prove $S_N[A_N]$ has a Hamiltonian path for all sufficiently large $N$.

problems.title: Hat Ising universality
problems.words: Magnets on a hat tiling should behave at their critical point exactly like magnets on a square grid.
problems.math: Prove the hat-graph Ising model has critical exponents $\beta=1/8$, $\gamma=7/4$, $\nu=1$.

problems.title: Counting Prime Nim losses
problems.words: Show the losing positions of Prime Nim thin out at a precise power rate.
problems.math: Prove $|L\cap[1,x]|=x^{\alpha+o(1)}$ for some $\alpha$ and compute it.

problems.title: Primes x² + y³ with prime inputs
problems.words: Show infinitely many primes are a square of a prime plus a cube of a prime.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many primes of the form $p^2+q^3$ with $p,q$ prime.

problems.title: Ambidextrous 3D sofa
problems.words: Find the largest solid that can turn either left or right at the end of a square pipe.
problems.math: Maximize volume over solids admissible for both the left and right turns of the $1\times1$ corridor.

problems.title: Hard-hat transition
problems.words: Show the gas of non-overlapping hats freezes abruptly at some density.
problems.math: Prove the hard-hat lattice gas has a first-order phase transition in the activity.

problems.title: Analytic hyperoperations
problems.words: Build one smooth family of operations from addition up through exponentiation that is analytic in all inputs.
problems.math: Construct $a[s]b$, real-analytic in $(s,a,b)$ for $s\in[1,3]$, $a>1$, $b>0$, satisfying the recursion law and matching $+,\times,\uparrow$.

problems.title: Infinitely many prime squared squares
problems.words: Show there are infinitely many perfect squared squares whose pieces all have prime sides.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many perfect squared squares with all component sides prime.

problems.title: Divisor-balanced primes
problems.words: Show infinitely many primes p have p − 1 and p + 1 with the same number of divisors.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ with $d(p-1)=d(p+1)$.

problems.title: Hat billiard scarring
problems.words: Show high-frequency waves in a hat-shaped room do not spread out evenly.
problems.math: Prove quantum unique ergodicity fails for the hat polygon: some subsequence of eigenfunctions has a non-uniform limit measure.

problems.title: Carmichael numbers with prime digit sum
problems.words: Show infinitely many Carmichael numbers have a digit sum that is prime.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many Carmichael numbers $n$ with $s_{10}(n)$ prime.

problems.title: Square-sum expansion
problems.words: Show the square-sum graph (on its large connected piece) is a good expander.
problems.math: Prove the giant component of $S_N$ has spectral gap at least $(\log N)^{-C}$.

problems.title: Keller maps with integer fibers
problems.words: Show no Jacobian-conjecture counterexample with integer coefficients is injective on integer points but not invertible.
problems.math: Prove every Keller map $F\in\mathbb{Z}[x,y,z]^3$ injective on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ is a polynomial automorphism of $\mathbb{C}^3$.

problems.title: Square-sum clique minors
problems.words: Find the largest complete graph that can be formed by contracting parts of the square-sum graph.
problems.math: Determine the order of growth of the Hadwiger number $h(S_N)$.

problems.title: Hat Ising critical line
problems.words: Ising models on a hat tiling and its dual should be exactly related at their critical points. Prove the duality relation holds rigorously.
problems.math: For the ferromagnetic Ising model on the hat graph $G$ and its planar dual $G^*$, prove $\sinh(2\beta_c(G))\sinh(2\beta_c(G^*))=1$.

problems.title: The spectre is not spectral
problems.words: Show the spectre, a curved tile that cannot tile by translations, has no orthogonal basis of exponentials, as Fuglede's conjecture predicts.
problems.math: Prove there is no $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ such that $\{e^{2\pi i\lambda\cdot x}\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is an orthogonal basis of $L^2$ of the spectre domain.

problems.title: Spanning trees inside the prime-sum graph
problems.words: Show every balanced tree of bounded degree on 2n vertices can be laid out on 1 to 2n so all its edges sum to primes.
problems.math: Prove that for every $\Delta$ there is $n_0$ such that every tree on $2n\ge n_0$ vertices with maximum degree $\le\Delta$ and bipartition classes of size $n$ is a spanning subgraph of the prime-sum graph on $[2n]$.

problems.title: Square-plus-one orbits avoid small primes
problems.words: Show that infinitely many starting numbers have square-plus-one sequences that never fall below their start.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many $n$ with $Q^k(n)\ge n$ for all $k\ge1$.

problems.title: 5n+1 largest-factor convergence
problems.words: Prove every orbit of the 5n+1 largest-factor map ends in a loop.
problems.math: For $f_5(n)=n/2$ (even), $P(5n+1)$ (odd), prove every orbit is eventually periodic.

problems.title: Hat dimer heights
problems.words: Random pairings of neighbouring hat tiles have a "height" landscape. Show it looks like the standard random surface at large scales.
problems.math: Prove the height function of uniform dimer covers of growing hat patches converges to a multiple of the Gaussian free field, and compute the multiple.

problems.title: Two colors for square sums, avoiding triangles
problems.words: Show every way to 2-color 1 to N, for large N, makes three same-colored numbers whose pairwise sums are all squares.
problems.math: Prove for large $N$ every 2-coloring of $[N]$ has a monochromatic triangle in $S_N$.

problems.title: Keller maps are invertible over Q in dimension 3, degree ≤ 4
problems.words: Show no Jacobian-conjecture counterexample exists in 3D up to degree 4 with rational coefficients.
problems.math: Prove every Keller map $F\in\mathbb{Q}[x,y,z]^3$ with $\deg F\le4$ is invertible.

problems.title: Spectre is a quasicrystal ground state
problems.words: Find a finite-range pair potential whose only zero-temperature arrangement is the spectre tiling.
problems.math: Construct a finite-range rotation-invariant pair potential for which every ground state is a spectre tiling, and prove it.

problems.title: Prime Nim with two piles
problems.words: Give an exact rule for who wins two-pile Prime Nim (remove a prime from one pile).
problems.math: Characterize $\{(a,b): G(a)\oplus G(b)=0\}$ via a formula for the Grundy function $G$ of Prime Nim.

problems.title: Integer Keller collisions
problems.words: Show any Jacobian-conjecture counterexample must send two different integer points to the same place.
problems.math: Prove every non-invertible Keller map in $\mathbb{Z}[x_1,\dots,x_n]^n$ is non-injective on $\mathbb{Z}^n$.

problems.title: Seven-free Carmichael numbers
problems.words: Show infinitely many Carmichael numbers have no digit 7.
problems.math: Prove there are infinitely many Carmichael numbers with no digit 7 in base 10.

problems.title: Firefighter on the hat tiling
problems.words: Find the exact average number of firefighters per turn needed to contain any fire on a hat tiling.
problems.math: Determine $\inf\{f: f\text{ firefighters per turn (averaged) contain every finite fire on the hat graph}\}$.

problems.title: Keller maps in dimension 3 of degree 5
problems.words: Show no Jacobian-conjecture counterexample exists in 3D with degree exactly 5 and rational coefficients.
problems.math: Prove every Keller map $F\in\mathbb{Q}[x,y,z]^3$ with $\deg F=5$ is invertible.

problems.title: Minimal degree of a Jacobian counterexample
problems.words: The 2026 counterexamples have degree 7. Find the smallest degree any 3D counterexample can have.
problems.math: Determine $\min\{\deg F: F:\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ non-invertible Keller map$\}$.

problems.title: SOF Collatz is undecidable in general
problems.words: Show some natural family of smallest-factor Collatz maps has an undecidable reach-1 question.
problems.math: Prove the problem "given $a,b$, does every orbit of $n\mapsto n/2$ or $\mathrm{spf}(an+b)$ reach 1?" is undecidable.

problems.title: Prime Nim is periodic in base 2
problems.words: Show the Grundy values of Prime Nim follow a pattern that a finite machine reads off the binary digits, or prove none exists.
problems.math: Decide whether the Grundy function of Prime Nim is $2$-automatic.

problems.title: Square-sum chromatic number
problems.words: Find exactly how many colors the infinite square-sum graph needs.
problems.math: Determine $\chi(S_\infty)$ exactly.

problems.title: Hat random walk return
problems.words: Find the exact probability that a random walk on hat tiles returns to its start within n steps, asymptotically.
problems.math: Prove $p_{2n}(o,o)\sim c/n$ on the hat graph and compute $c$ exactly.

problems.title: Spectre dimers are critical
problems.words: Show random pairings of spectre tiles have long-range correlations, like the square grid.
problems.math: Prove dimer correlations on the spectre tiling decay as a power law with exponent 2.

problems.title: Seven-free primes have a bounded gap
problems.words: Show infinitely many pairs of seven-free primes lie within a fixed distance of each other.
problems.math: Prove $\liminf(q_{n+1}-q_n)<\infty$ where $q_n$ enumerates the 7-free primes.

problems.title: Square-sum Ramsey numbers
problems.words: Find the exact point at which every 2-coloring of 1 to N contains a same-colored square-sum clique of size 4.
problems.math: Determine $\min\{N: \text{every 2-coloring of }[N]\text{ has a monochromatic }K_4\text{ in }S_N\}$, or prove none exists.

problems.title: Optimal 3D origami
problems.words: For every 3D shape, find the smallest sheet of paper that folds into it.
problems.math: Give a characterization, with an algorithm, of the minimal-area square that folds into any given polyhedral surface.

problems.title: Prime Nim Grundy values are unbounded in density
problems.words: Show each Grundy value of Prime Nim appears with a precise positive density, and compute them all.
problems.math: Prove $d_k=\lim\frac1x\#\{n\le x: G(n)=k\}$ exists for every $k$ and give a formula.

problems.title: Hadwiger's true constant
problems.words: If graphs needing many colors need not contain a full complete-graph minor, find how large a complete minor they must contain.
problems.math: Find $c^*=\liminf_{t}\min\{h(G)/t:\chi(G)\ge t\}$, where $h$ is the Hadwiger number.

problems.title: Random hat parking
problems.words: Drop hat tiles at random without overlap until no more fit. What fraction gets covered?
problems.math: Compute the jamming density of random sequential adsorption of hats (random rotations from the kite grid) in the plane.

problems.title: The 4p+1 funnel, almost always
problems.words: Show almost every prime falls into the eight-prime loop of the 4p + 1 map.
problems.math: Prove the set of primes whose $p\mapsto P(4p+1)$ orbit enters the 8-cycle has relative density 1 among primes.

problems.title: Affine prime maps, quantitative
problems.words: Show that for the map p ↦ largest prime factor of 3p + 4, almost every prime reaches its loop within about log log p steps.
problems.math: For $p\mapsto P(3p+4)$, prove that for all but $o(\pi(x))$ primes $p\le x$ the orbit of $p$ enters its (unique observed) 7-cycle within $C\log\log p$ steps.

problems.title: Square-sum triangle-free density
problems.words: Find the largest fraction of 1 to N you can keep with no three numbers whose pairwise sums are all perfect squares.
problems.math: Determine $\lim_{N}\frac1N\max\{|A|:A\subseteq[N],\ A\text{ contains no triangle of }S_N\}$.

problems.title: Squares of seven-free primes
problems.words: Show infinitely many primes have no digit 7 in themselves or in their squares.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ with neither $p$ nor $p^2$ containing the decimal digit 7.

problems.title: Sofa constant digits
problems.words: Show the digits of Gerver's sofa area do not end in a repeating pattern in base 2 either, and give an explicit irrationality measure bound.
problems.math: Prove $\mu_G$ is irrational with irrationality measure $\le 100$.

problems.title: Hat Hofstadter at golden flux
problems.words: Thread a magnetic flux through each hat tile equal to the golden ratio. Show the resulting energy spectrum is a zero-measure Cantor set.
problems.math: For the magnetic tight-binding Hamiltonian on the hat graph with flux $\phi=(\sqrt5-1)/2$ per kite, prove $\sigma(H)$ is a Cantor set of Lebesgue measure zero.

problems.title: Hat dominoes freeze
problems.words: Random domino-style pairings of hat tiles inside a large region with a fixed boundary develop a frozen outer zone. Find the shape of the boundary between frozen and random regions.
problems.math: For uniform perfect matchings of the hat graph on regions $L\cdot\Omega$, prove an arctic curve exists and identify it for $\Omega$ a regular hexagon.

problems.title: Spectre billiards ergodic
problems.words: Billiards inside a spectre-shaped room with curved walls should be chaotic. Prove the billiard flow is ergodic.
problems.math: Prove the billiard flow in the spectre (with its circular-arc edges) is ergodic with respect to Liouville measure.

problems.title: Seven-free values of n²+1
problems.words: Show infinitely many n make n² + 1 a prime with no digit 7, or at least a product of two such primes.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many $n$ with $n^2+1=q_1q_2$, $q_i$ primes free of the digit 7.

problems.title: Quasi-independence of square-plus-one steps
problems.words: Show the largest prime factors of n² + 1 and (n + 1)² + 1 are nearly independent in size.

problems.title: Prime Nim's mod-3 bias
problems.words: Losing pile sizes in Prime Nim are about three times as likely to be 1 mod 3 as 0 mod 3. Find the exact limiting proportions.
problems.math: For the prime subtraction game, prove the limits $\lim_x\#\{n\le x:G(n)=0,\ n\equiv r\ (3)\}/\#\{n\le x:G(n)=0\}$ exist for $r=0,1,2$, and determine them.

problems.title: Square losses in Prime Nim
problems.words: Many perfect squares (1, 9, 25, 49, 100, 121, …) are losing Prime Nim positions. Show there are infinitely many.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many perfect squares $k^2$ satisfy $G(k^2)=0$ in the prime subtraction game.

problems.title: Increasing square-plus-one factors
problems.words: Among the largest prime factors of n² + 1 for n up to N, find the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
problems.math: Determine $\theta$ with $L(N)=N^{\theta+o(1)}$, where $L(N)$ is the longest strictly increasing subsequence of $(P(n^2+1))_{n\le N}$.

problems.title: Density of Grundy value one in Prime Nim
problems.words: Show the pile sizes with Grundy value exactly 1 in Prime Nim have a definite density, and that it is positive.
problems.math: For the prime subtraction game, prove $\lim_x\frac1x\#\{n\le x:G(n)=1\}$ exists and is positive.

problems.title: Gerver constant is transcendental
problems.words: Show the area of Gerver's sofa is not a root of any polynomial with integer coefficients.
problems.math: Prove $\mu_G\approx2.2195$ is transcendental.

problems.title: The 4p+1 funnel
problems.words: Map a prime p to the largest prime factor of 4p + 1. Every prime tested falls into one loop of eight primes. Prove all do.
problems.math: Prove every orbit of $p\mapsto P(4p+1)$ on primes enters the cycle $5\to7\to29\to13\to53\to71\to19\to11\to5$.

problems.title: Affine prime maps all settle
problems.words: Fix whole numbers a and b. Send a prime p to the largest prime factor of ap + b. Every case tested falls into a loop. Prove this always happens.
problems.math: Prove that for all fixed integers $a\ge2$, $b\ge1$, every orbit of $p\mapsto P(ap+b)$ on primes is eventually periodic.

problems.title: The 7p+4 dozen
problems.words: Under p ↦ largest prime factor of 7p + 4, every tested prime ends in one loop of length 12. Prove all do.
problems.math: Prove every orbit of $p\mapsto P(7p+4)$ on primes enters a single cycle of length 12, and identify it.

problems.title: Keller maps classification
problems.words: List every Jacobian-conjecture counterexample in 3D, up to symmetry.
problems.math: Classify all non-invertible Keller maps $\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ up to composition with polynomial automorphisms.

problems.title: Hat-tiling site percolation is irrational
problems.words: The critical probability for percolation on the hat tiling is about 0.5442. Prove it is irrational.
problems.math: Prove $p_c^{\mathrm{site}}$ of the hat-tiling dual graph is irrational.

problems.title: Irrationality of the hat percolation threshold, bond
problems.words: The bond-percolation threshold on the hat tiling's edges is about 0.7982. Prove it is irrational.
problems.math: Prove $p_c^{\mathrm{bond}}$ for the hat tiling's edge graph is irrational.

problems.title: Hyperoperation transcendence
problems.words: Show values of the natural hyperoperation at non-integer ranks are algebraically independent.
problems.math: Prove $\{2[s]3: s\in\mathbb{Q}\cap(2,3)\}$ is algebraically independent over $\mathbb{Q}$.

problems.title: Spectre quantum walk spreading
problems.words: A quantum particle hopping on the spectre tiling should spread at a rate strictly between localization and free motion. Compute the exponent.
problems.math: For $H$ the adjacency operator of a spectre tiling and $\psi_0=\delta_o$, prove $\langle|X|^2\rangle_T\asymp T^{2\beta}$ and determine $\beta$.

problems.title: Prime points on a quartic threefold
problems.words: Count prime solutions of x⁴ + y⁴ + z⁴ = w⁴ + 2 up to size X, and find the asymptotic.
problems.math: Find the asymptotic number of prime 4-tuples $\le X$ with $x^4+y^4+z^4=w^4+2$, or prove there are finitely many.

problems.title: AKLT on the hat
problems.words: Show the AKLT quantum spin model placed on a hat tiling has an energy gap above its ground state.
problems.math: For the AKLT Hamiltonian on the vertex graph of a hat tiling (spin $d(v)/2$ at vertex $v$), prove a uniform spectral gap on finite patches.

problems.title: Three loops for 2p+3
problems.words: Under p ↦ largest prime factor of 2p + 3, every tested prime ends in one of three loops. Prove there are no others.
problems.math: Prove every orbit of $p\mapsto P(2p+3)$ on primes enters one of the cycles $\{3\}$, $\{5,13,29,61\}$, $\{43,89,181,73,149\}$.

problems.title: Gerver sofa algebraic independence of its angles
problems.words: Gerver's sofa is built from two special angles. Show they are algebraically independent over the rationals.
problems.math: Prove the two transcendental switching angles $\varphi\approx0.0392$ and $\theta\approx0.6813$ in Gerver's construction are algebraically independent over $\mathbb{Q}$.

problems.title: Escaping p²+p+1
problems.words: Start at 2 and repeatedly take the largest prime factor of p² + p + 1. Show the sequence grows without bound.
problems.math: Prove the orbit of $2$ under $p\mapsto P(p^2+p+1)$ is unbounded.

problems.title: Gerver sofa is not periodic in its digits
problems.words: Show the digits of Gerver's sofa area never fall into a repeating pattern in any base, and are not "too well" approximable.
problems.math: Prove the irrationality measure of $\mu_G$ equals 2.

problems.title: Partition numbers contain a 7
problems.words: Show that from some point on, every partition number has a 7 among its digits.
problems.math: Prove there is $N$ such that the decimal expansion of $p(n)$ contains the digit 7 for all $n\ge N$.

problems.title: Prime Nim complexity
problems.words: Decide exactly how hard it is to tell if a Prime Nim pile is losing: show it can't be done fast without unproven assumptions.
problems.math: Prove, unconditionally, that deciding $G(n)=0$ in Prime Nim requires time $(\log n)^{\omega(1)}$.
